Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance (PERMANOVA)

Source: R/permanova.r
permanova.Rd

Tests whether sample metadata, such as treatment groups, explain the differences between samples in a distance matrix. Gives the same table as vegan::adonis2(): degrees of freedom, sums of squares, \(R^2\), and pseudo-\(F\) statistics, with permutation p-values. Computes them in parallel C, straight from the distances, without the \(n \times n\) matrices that adonis2() builds for every permutation.

Usage

permanova(
  dm,
  groups,
  data = NULL,
  formula = NULL,
  by = "overall",
  permutations = 999L,
  strata = NULL,
  seed = 0L,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

dm

A dist object, such as from beta_div() or bray(), or a symmetric numeric matrix of distances. Must not contain NAs or negative values. Alternatively, as in vegan::adonis2(), a formula with the distances on its left-hand side and the terms to test on its right, such as dm ~ treatment, in place of dm and formula; the metadata may then be given second, as in permanova(dm ~ treatment, meta).

groups

The one variable to test: a vector or factor with one value per sample, matched to the samples in dm by name when both are named, else in the same order as dm. Or, when data is given, the name of one of its columns (or a vector with one value per row of data). Categories (factor, character, or logical) or a numeric covariate. The same as formula = ~ groups. Give groups or formula, not both.

data

Sample metadata: a data frame with one row per sample, holding the columns named in groups, formula, or strata. Rows are matched to the samples in dm by row name, and rows for other samples are ignored; without row names, they must be in the same order as dm. Default: NULL.

formula

Instead of groups, for models of several variables: a one-sided formula naming the variables in data to test, such as ~ treatment or ~ treatment * site + ph. Factors, numeric covariates, and interactions are all allowed. Wrap variables in Condition() to remove their effect before the other terms are tested, as in vegan::dbrda(). A left-hand side, if given, is ignored. Give groups or formula: there is no default model (as in vegan::adonis2()). Default: NULL.

by

How to test the terms of formula:

  • 'overall': One test of all the terms together. The default, as in adonis2() since vegan 2.6-8; earlier versions of adonis2() defaulted to by = "terms", so compare with those using by = 'terms'.

  • 'terms': Each term in turn, after the ones before it (sequential, or type I, sums of squares). Their order in formula matters.

  • 'margin': Each term after all the others (marginal sums of squares), for the terms that can be dropped without breaking marginality: in ~ a * b, only a:b.

  • 'onedf': Each column of the model matrix in turn, such as each contrast of a factor.

permutations

The number of permutations. Default: 999. Alternatively, a matrix with one permutation of 1:n per row, as from permute::shuffleSet(), to use instead of random ones.

strata

Permute samples only within these groups (blocks), for designs such as repeated measures. With data, the name of one of its columns, or a vector with one value per row of data. Without data, a vector with one value per sample, matched to the samples by name when it has names, otherwise in the same order. Default: NULL (free permutation).

seed

An integer seed for the random permutations. The same seed gives the same p-values. Default: 0

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), will use all logical CPU cores.

Value

A list of class c("ecodive_permanova", "ecodive_test"), which prints as a summary and the table of terms. as.data.frame() gives its first four fields as one row, with the same columns as ecodive's other permutation tests. The first four fields are for the model as a whole, whatever by is (the "Model" row of by = 'overall'):

  • statistic: The model's pseudo-\(F\), named F.

  • p_value: Its permutation p-value.

  • z: Its standardized effect size, (F - mean(f_perm)) / sd(f_perm), as summary(vegan::permustats()).

  • n_perm: The number of permutations.

  • r2: The model's \(R^2\): the proportion of the total sum of squares it explains.

  • table: The table of vegan::adonis2(): a data frame (of class "anova", so it prints like stats::anova() tables) with one row per term tested (or one "Model" row when by = 'overall'), then "Residual" and "Total" rows. When formula has Condition() terms, a "Conditional" row comes first. Its columns are Df (degrees of freedom), SumOfSqs (sum of squares), R2 (proportion of the total sum of squares), F (pseudo-\(F\)), and Pr(>F) (permutation p-value). Its attribute f_perm is a matrix of the \(F\) statistics of each permutation (rows) for each test (columns), as adonis2()'s F.perm.

  • by: The by used.

  • permutation: How samples were permuted: 'free', 'within strata', or 'supplied matrix'.

Attribute f_perm holds the model's \(F\) for each permutation.

Details

Method

PERMANOVA (Anderson 2001) partitions the variation in the distances among the terms of a linear model, following McArdle & Anderson (2001): with \(A\) the squared distances, \(G = -\frac{1}{2}JAJ\) Gower's centred matrix, and \(H\) the hat matrix of the (centred) model, a model's sum of squares is \(trace(HGH)\), out of a total \(trace(G) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i<j}d_{ij}^2\). The pseudo-\(F\) of a term with \(q\) degrees of freedom is $$F = \frac{SS_{term} / q}{SS_{residual} / (n - 1 - p)}$$ where \(p\) counts the degrees of freedom of the whole model. For each permutation, the samples' distances are shuffled relative to the metadata and \(F\) is recomputed. The p-value is the proportion of permutations, counting the observed one, with an \(F\) at least as large: \((1 + \#\{F_{perm} \ge F\}) / (1 + permutations)\). As in adonis2(), permuted statistics within sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) of the observed one count as ties.

Partial models, with Condition() terms, follow vegan::dbrda() and vegan::anova.cca()'s default "reduced" model: the conditions' effect is removed from the distances, and the residuals are permuted.

Every term is tested with the same permutations of the (conditioned) distances, as in adonis2(). PERMANOVA+ for PRIMER instead permutes the residuals of a separate reduced model for each term (Freedman & Lane 1983), which can give slightly different p-values for terms after the first.

Speed and memory

With \(Q\) an orthonormal basis of the model matrix, \(trace(HGH) = \sum_c q_c^T G q_c\), and each \(q^T G q = -\sum_{i<j} q_i q_j d_{ij}^2\) is read straight from dm. A permutation of the samples permutes the rows of \(Q\), so each permutation costs one pass over the distances, shared by many vectors at once, with no \(n \times n\) matrix. For a single factor, the sum of squares within groups is summed over the pairs of samples in the same group instead (Anderson 2001), which is faster still. Permutations run in parallel.

Reproducibility

The permutations come from seed, not from R's random number generator, so set.seed() has no effect, and each permutation has a random number stream of its own. P-values are identical from run to run and for any number of cpus. The random permutations differ from adonis2()'s, so p-values agree with it only up to sampling error, unless the same permutations matrix is given to both.

Differences from adonis2()

  • permanova() takes distances, not a community table: compute them first with beta_div() or a metric function such as bray(). One variable can be given as groups, like ecodive's other tests; several as formula, with data. adonis2()'s style, permanova(dm ~ terms, data), also works.

  • adonis2()'s table is the table field, and its permuted \(F\) statistics (F.perm) are attr(res$table, 'f_perm').

  • A term with no degrees of freedom left (aliased with the terms before it) has no \(F\) or p-value (NA), where adonis2() reports an infinite or undefined \(F\).

  • strata permutes freely within strata. For other restricted designs, pass a permutations matrix from permute::shuffleSet().

  • When there are fewer possible permutations than requested, adonis2() (via permute) runs each of them once instead. permanova() always draws random permutations.

References

Anderson, M. J. (2001). A new method for non-parametric multivariate analysis of variance. Austral Ecology, 26(1), 32-46. doi:10.1111/j.1442-9993.2001.01070.pp.x

Freedman, D., & Lane, D. (1983). A nonstochastic interpretation of reported significance levels. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 1(4), 292-298. doi:10.1080/07350015.1983.10509354

McArdle, B. H., & Anderson, M. J. (2001). Fitting multivariate models to community data: a comment on distance-based redundancy analysis. Ecology, 82(1), 290-297. doi:10.1890/0012-9658(2001)082[0290:FMMTCD]2.0.CO;2

See also

dbrda(), beta_div(), pcoa()

Examples

    # 30 samples in three treatment groups. The 'high' group has more
    # of the first five genera.
    set.seed(1)
    counts <- matrix(rpois(30 * 20, 5), 30, 20)
    rownames(counts) <- paste0('S', 1:30)
    meta <- data.frame(
      row.names = rownames(counts),
      treatment = rep(c('ctrl', 'low', 'high'), each = 10),
      ph        = round(rnorm(30, 7, 0.3), 1) )
    high <- meta$treatment == 'high'
    counts[high, 1:5] <- counts[high, 1:5] + 5

    dm <- bray(counts)

    # Does treatment explain differences in community composition?
    res <- permanova(dm, 'treatment', meta)
    res
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA)
#> 
#> F = 3.442, p = 0.001, z = 8.275
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Model R2 = 0.2032. Model tested as a whole:
#> 
#>          Df SumOfSqs     R2     F Pr(>F)    
#> Model     2   0.1813 0.2032 3.442  0.001 ***
#> Residual 27   0.7111 0.7968                 
#> Total    29   0.8924 1.0000                 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

    # The same, with the groups as a vector.
    permanova(dm, meta$treatment)
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA)
#> 
#> F = 3.442, p = 0.001, z = 8.275
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Model R2 = 0.2032. Model tested as a whole:
#> 
#>          Df SumOfSqs     R2     F Pr(>F)    
#> Model     2   0.1813 0.2032 3.442  0.001 ***
#> Residual 27   0.7111 0.7968                 
#> Total    29   0.8924 1.0000                 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

    # F, p-value and z-score as one row, and adonis2()'s table.
    as.data.frame(res)
#>        test stat_name statistic p_value        z n_perm
#> 1 permanova         F  3.442219   0.001 8.274905    999
    res$table
#> Permutation test for PERMANOVA
#> Model tested as a whole
#> Permutation: free
#> Number of permutations: 999
#> 
#>          Df SumOfSqs      R2      F Pr(>F)    
#> Model     2  0.18132 0.20317 3.4422  0.001 ***
#> Residual 27  0.71110 0.79683                  
#> Total    29  0.89242 1.00000                  
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

    # Several variables: a formula. Each term in turn, after the ones
    # before it.
    permanova(dm, data = meta, formula = ~ treatment + ph, by = 'terms')
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA)
#> 
#> F = 2.415, p = 0.001, z = 5.633
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Model R2 = 0.2179. Terms added sequentially (first to last):
#> 
#>           Df SumOfSqs     R2     F Pr(>F)    
#> treatment  2   0.1813 0.2032 3.377  0.001 ***
#> ph         1   0.0131 0.0147 0.490  0.925    
#> Residual  26   0.6980 0.7821                 
#> Total     29   0.8924 1.0000                 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

    # The same, in adonis2()'s style.
    permanova(dm ~ treatment + ph, meta, by = 'terms')
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA)
#> 
#> F = 2.415, p = 0.001, z = 5.633
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Model R2 = 0.2179. Terms added sequentially (first to last):
#> 
#>           Df SumOfSqs     R2     F Pr(>F)    
#> treatment  2   0.1813 0.2032 3.377  0.001 ***
#> ph         1   0.0131 0.0147 0.490  0.925    
#> Residual  26   0.6980 0.7821                 
#> Total     29   0.8924 1.0000                 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

    # pH, after removing the effect of treatment.
    permanova(dm, data = meta, formula = ~ ph + Condition(treatment))
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA)
